skill.name: firecrawl-scrape
skill.description: Scrape one or more URLs with Firecrawl and return clean, LLM-ready page content. Supports JavaScript-rendered pages, main-content extraction, links, screenshots, HTML, JSON, and targeted page questions.
skill.summary: Scrapes specific web pages with Firecrawl and returns clean markdown or requested formats.
skill.author: firecrawl

security_audit.summary: All static findings are documentation artifacts in SKILL.md, including command examples, inline option names, example.com URLs, and sibling markdown links. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or executable code was found in the reviewed file.

static_findings.snippet: ```bash
| `-f, --format <formats>` | Output formats: markdown, html, rawHtml, links, screenshot, json |
| `-Q, --query <prompt>`   | Ask a question about the page content (5 credits)                |
| `-H`                     | Include HTTP headers in output                                   |
| `--only-main-content`    | Strip nav, footer, sidebar — main content only                   |
| `--wait-for <ms>`        | Wait for JS rendering before scraping                            |
| `--include-tags <tags>`  | Only include these HTML tags                                     |
| `--exclude-tags <tags>`  | Exclude these HTML tags                                          |
| `-o, --output <path>`    | Output file path                                                 |
- **Prefer plain scrape over `--query`.** Scrape to a file, then use `grep`, `head`, or read the mar
- **Try scrape before interact.** Scrape handles static pages and JS-rendered SPAs. Only escalate to
- Multiple URLs are scraped concurrently — check `firecrawl --status` for your concurrency limit.
- Single format outputs raw content. Multiple formats (e.g., `--format markdown,links`) output JSON.
- Always quote URLs — shell interprets `?` and `&` as special characters.
- Naming convention: `.firecrawl/{site}-{path}.md`
firecrawl scrape https://example.com https://example.com/blog https://example.com/docs
firecrawl scrape "https://example.com/pricing" --query "What is the enterprise plan price?"

content.user_title: Scrape Web Pages Into Clean Markdown
content.value_statement: Web pages can be hard to extract cleanly when scripts render important content. This skill uses Firecrawl to scrape URLs into LLM-ready markdown and optional formats.
actual_capabilities: Scrapes one or more URLs with the Firecrawl CLI.
Saves clean markdown to local .firecrawl files.
Requests main-content extraction to reduce navigation and footer noise.
Waits before scraping pages that need JavaScript rendering.
Returns optional formats such as links, screenshots, HTML, raw HTML, and JSON.
Asks targeted questions about a page through Firecrawl query mode.
limitations: It requires the Firecrawl CLI or npx Firecrawl command to be available.
It depends on Firecrawl service access and any required account credits.
It only works for URLs reachable by Firecrawl.
Interactive actions need a separate interact workflow.

use_cases.title: Research Source Capture
use_cases.description: Researchers can scrape source pages into markdown before summarizing or extracting claims.

use_cases.title: Product Page Review
use_cases.description: Product teams can collect pricing, feature, or FAQ content from specific pages.

use_cases.title: Developer Documentation Intake
use_cases.description: Developers can pull clean docs content from a URL before analysis or migration.

prompt_templates.title: Scrape One Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Scrape https://example.com/docs into clean markdown and save the result under .firecrawl.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Main Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Scrape https://example.com/blog with main content only, then summarize the page sections.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Multiple Pages
prompt_templates.prompt: Scrape these three URLs concurrently and compare their main topics: https://example.com, https://example.com/blog, https://example.com/docs.

prompt_templates.title: Ask A Targeted Question
prompt_templates.prompt: Scrape https://example.com/pricing and answer this question from the page: What is included in the enterprise plan?

output_examples.input: Scrape a product page and summarize it.
output: Saved clean markdown for the page.
Returned the page title, key sections, and important links.
Provided a short summary of pricing and feature details.

output_examples.input: Compare documentation and blog pages from one site.
output: Separated shared topics from page-specific details.
Flagged links that may need deeper review.

output_examples.input: Ask a focused question about a pricing page.
output: Used query mode for the requested page.
Answered only from the scraped page content.
Noted when the page did not include the requested detail.

best_practices: Quote URLs before running scrape commands.
Save full markdown first when you need detailed analysis.
Use query mode only for narrow questions because it uses extra credits.
anti_patterns: Do not scrape pages without permission or a valid reason.
Do not use query mode when full page review is required.
Do not store sensitive page captures in shared folders.

faq.question: Does this skill need Firecrawl installed?
faq.answer: Yes. It needs the Firecrawl CLI or npx command available to the agent.

faq.question: Can it handle JavaScript-rendered pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can wait before scraping so rendered content has time to load.

faq.question: Can it scrape multiple URLs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can scrape several URLs concurrently when Firecrawl allows the requested concurrency.

faq.question: What output formats are supported?
faq.answer: It can request markdown, links, screenshots, HTML, raw HTML, and JSON.

faq.question: Is WebFetch required?
faq.answer: No. The skill uses Firecrawl commands for page extraction.

faq.question: Should I use query mode for every page?
faq.answer: No. Use query mode for focused questions because it costs extra Firecrawl credits.
